tax_note: Retail cannabis sales carry a 37% excise tax plus state and local retail sales tax; medical-endorsed retailers' sales to registered patients are exempt from the excise tax until June 30, 2029 (RCW 69.50.535; WA Department of Revenue).
summary: Washington was one of the first two states to open adult-use stores, in July 2014, and its market has been shrinking since peaking during the pandemic. Retail sales reported to the Liquor and Cannabis Board fell from $1.50 billion in fiscal 2021 to $1.19 billion in fiscal 2025 (July 2024 to June 2025), the fourth straight annual decline. Falling flower prices, a cap on store licenses, the country's highest cannabis excise rate at 37%, and competition from cheaper Oregon stores across the Columbia River all weigh on revenue. King County, home to Seattle, accounts for the largest share of sales.

faq.q: How much cannabis does Washington sell a year?
faq.a: Licensed retailers reported $1.19 billion in sales in fiscal 2025 (July 2024 to June 2025), according to the Liquor and Cannabis Board.
Yes. Annual sales have fallen every fiscal year since the $1.50 billion peak in fiscal 2021.
